root_cause.text: A race condition in filemap_map_pages() where end_pgoff is calculated after fetching the folio, allowing a concurrent truncation to shrink i_size below the folio’s start index, which causes the nr_pages calculation to underflow (wrap to a large unsigned value) and map beyond the folio boundary.
root_cause.evidence: The CVE description explicitly shows the race: CPU 0 calls next_uptodate_folio() with the old end_pgoff, then CPU 1 shrinks i_size, then CPU 0 reads the new i_size and computes min(end, end_pgoff) < xas.xa_index, leading to nr_pages overflow. The patch moves the file_end and end_pgoff computation before next_uptodate_folio() to prevent this.

agent_logs.evidence_points: The CVE description explicitly shows the race: CPU 0 calls next_uptodate_folio() with the old end_pgoff, then CPU 1 shrinks i_size, then CPU 0 reads the new i_size and computes min(end, end_pgoff) < xas.xa_index, leading to nr_pages overflow. Declaration of mmap_miss variables; part of the same code block and indirectly involved in the mapping logic after the race.

Fetches the folio using the current (possibly stale) end_pgoff before i_size is rechecked, enabling the race.
Null check for the fetched folio; control flow depends on this, but the race is about the folio being beyond the new i_size.
Early exit when folio is NULL; not directly vulnerable but part of the same logic block.
Reads i_size after folio fetch; if truncation occurs between fetch and this read, file_end may be smaller than the folio's start index.

vuln_statements.explanation: Fetches the folio using the current end_pgoff before i_size is rechecked. A concurrent truncation after this fetch can shrink i_size below the folio's start index, enabling the race.
